tasks.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: ONE isolated supplementary view of an existing twin-pilot spacecraft main instrument desk, for an eight-view image-to-3D input set. This is a 2D design view, not an implemented 3D model.
Reference image 1 is the binding object identity: its upper-left quadrant shows the operator-facing FRONT, upper-right true BACK, lower-left LEFT SIDE, lower-right RIGHT SIDE. Derive the requested camera view of this SAME manufactured object; do not redesign or combine the four quadrants in the output.
Preserve the exact warm ivory/graphite housing family, two sloping dark instrument banks with cyan graphics, narrow central service spine, and exactly TWO upright black joystick grips with bellows integrated in the operator-facing front lip, one per pilot station. Both grip tops remain below the upper display edge. Preserve the two slim square support columns and shallow bolted rectangular feet, the open knee/leg space, and the same panel outlines, vents, seams and fasteners wherever visible. A support or grip hidden by the new viewing angle should be physically occluded, not moved to make it visible. No third grip, loose stick, seat armrest, separate floor pedestal, extra screen bank or newly invented extension.
Provisional envelope is width 2.30m, height 1.16m, depth 0.90m. These are proportions only; do not print dimensions. No room, seats, hull, people, labels, text, arrows, dividing lines, watermark or branding.
Render the whole single object completely within the frame with generous white margins, on a plain pure white background. Use a clean industrial product reference rendering, even neutral studio lighting, sharp engineered edges, restrained subtle surface wear, no dramatic shadows obscuring form. Landscape composition. Only the one requested view appears in the image.

tasks.camera: Requested view: TRUE BOTTOM/UNDERSIDE, camera looking vertically straight upward from below the intact desk, orthographic parallel projection. Width is horizontal; operator-facing lip is at the BOTTOM, rear edge at the TOP. Show coherent underside panels, the underside of both shallow bolted feet and the two support connections with correct natural occlusion. The display graphics and joystick tops are on the far side and should NOT be relocated onto the underside. Do not invent extra legs, a full-width lower wall, central column, hanging cables or a second desktop. The feet and desk are one intact object, not an exploded view.
